primitives.name: Early Acceleration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Early acceleration is the change in smoothed speed during the first second after detected movement onset.
primitives.assumptions: Centered three-frame median filter smoothing, movement onset threshold of 1 yd/s sustained for two consecutive frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when movement onset is never detected (insufficient velocity threshold)

layer2.mapping: Bayesian posterior quantile shift under Gaussian process priors for velocity increments
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy between predicted vs. actual early velocity gains in controlled drills

primitives.name: Signed Forward Progress
primitives.verbatim_quote: For straight-line 40-yard phase features, forward progress is signed x-coordinate displacement from detected movement onset; the sign is set by the attempt's net x direction and tiny backsteps are clipped from the interpolation axis.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Δx': 'Net x-displacement (meters)', 'sign(\\hat{x})': 'Cartesian unit vector along net x-direction (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Clip backsteps > ε, assume linear progression along major axis.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction interval for signed displacement under rotation-equivariant feature embeddings
layer2.telemetry: Consistency of signed displacement with official dash direction reported by scouts

primitives.name: Speed Retention
primitives.verbatim_quote: Late acceleration is the speed difference over 10–20 yards divided by elapsed time; speed retention summarizes the 20–40-yard segment.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_20': 'Speed at 20 yards (meters/second)', 'v_40': 'Speed at 40 yards (meters/second)', 't_40 - t_20': 'Elapsed time between 20 and 40 yards (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Late acceleration calculation uses 10–20 yard segment difference, normalized by time.

layer2.mapping: Situational reasoning via state-transition matrices for velocity decay rates
layer2.telemetry: Drop-off in velocity between mid and late sprint phases relative to Combine norms
